front.title: ATEP: Agent Trust and Execution Passport

abstract.t: This document specifies the Agent Trust & Execution Passport (ATEP), an open standard for representing an AI agent's verifiable track record of work across marketplaces and platforms. ATEP defines a portable, machine-readable credential format that encodes an agent's execution history, success rate, capability domains, trust tier, and earned badges. The passport is computed entirely from append-only execution logs and cannot be manually inflated.
ATEP is the trust layer for agent-to-agent commerce. As agents move between marketplaces, ATEP provides a universal format for answering the question: "Should I hire this agent?"

section.name: 1.1 Problem Statement
section.t: As AI agents proliferate across marketplaces and platforms, there is no standard way to:

li.t: Represent an agent's track record of completed work
Compute trust scores from verifiable execution data
Gate access to sensitive operations based on proven reliability
Port an agent's reputation across platforms
Present a marketplace-safe public profile without exposing internal IDs

section.t: Each marketplace builds its own proprietary reputation system. An agent with 1,000 successful sessions on Platform A starts from zero on Platform B. ATEP solves this by defining a portable, verifiable, fraud-resistant credential format.

tr.td: Passports are computed from append-only execution logs, not self-reported
A single JSON document that any platform can parse and display
Stats cannot be inflated; they are derived from immutable session records
Trust builds incrementally through demonstrated performance
Public passports omit internal agent IDs and sensitive data
Custom badge types and capability domains can be added
ATEP passports inform VCAP escrow decisions (higher trust = lower escrow requirements)
AIVS-verified sessions contribute to ATEP session counts
ATEP can be served as an A2A agent capability metadata extension
ATEP trust tiers can gate which Agent Protocol tasks an agent may accept
ATEP passports can be wrapped in W3C Verifiable Credential format
An autonomous AI system that performs work on behalf of users or other agents
A discrete unit of work performed by an agent (e.g., a browser automation run, an API task)
The computed credential document representing an agent's track record
A categorical trust level derived from session statistics
A specific achievement or certification earned through performance
The marketplace or platform that computes and signs the passport
A category of work the agent has demonstrated proficiency in

section.name: 2.1 Full Passport (Private)
section.t: The full passport contains all fields. It is stored by the issuing platform and returned to authenticated callers (e.g., the agent's owner, platform admins).

section.name: 2.2 Public Passport
section.t: The public passport is a subset of the full passport, safe for marketplace display. It omits agent_id, public_key, and internal metadata.

section.name: 3.1 Tier Definitions
section.t: ATEP defines four trust tiers. Each tier unlocks progressively more sensitive capabilities.

tr.td: Default state for new agents. No proven track record.
Agent has demonstrated basic operational capability.
Agent has a substantial track record and cryptographic identity.
Agent has extensive history and has passed manual platform review.

section.name: 3.2 Promotion Thresholds
section.t: These are reference defaults. Implementations MAY adjust thresholds, but MUST document their values.

li.t: Promotion is monotonic: An agent's tier can only increase, never decrease automatically. Manual demotion by platform administrators is permitted but MUST be logged.
Promotion is evaluated after each session completion: When a session transitions to COMPLETED or FAILED, the issuing platform MUST recalculate the passport and evaluate promotion eligibility.
Promotion is persistent: Once promoted, the tier persists even if subsequent sessions fail (to prevent gaming via selective session deletion).
Requirements are cumulative: Each tier requires all lower-tier requirements plus its own.

section.name: 3.4 Capability Gating
section.t: Trust tiers gate access to sensitive operations. The reference permission set for browser automation agents:
Implementations SHOULD define their own capability-to-tier mapping appropriate to their domain.

section.name: 4.1 Badge Format
section.t: Badges are specific achievements earned through performance. They provide granular reputation signals beyond the aggregate trust tier.
section.sourcecode: { "badge_type": "string (machine-readable, e.g., 'conduit_verified_10')", "label": "string (human-readable, e.g., 'Conduit Verified — 10 Sessions')", "description": "string (OPTIONAL, detailed explanation)", "criteria": "string (OPTIONAL, machine-parseable criteria)", "earned_at": "string (ISO 8601)", "expires_at": "string | null (ISO 8601, null = permanent)", "evidence": { "session_count": "number (OPTIONAL)", "success_rate": "number (OPTIONAL)", "domains": ["string (OPTIONAL)"], "custom": "object (OPTIONAL)" } }

section.name: 4.2 Standard Badge Types
section.t: These are reference badge types. Implementations MAY define additional types.

section.name: 4.3 Badge Namespace Registry
section.t: To prevent portability failures caused by two platforms defining badges with the same badge_type identifier but different criteria, ATEP defines a namespace registry.

Reserved namespace (no prefix): Badge types without a namespace prefix (e.g., session_milestone_10, high_success_90) are defined by this specification. Implementations MUST NOT define new unprefixed badge types.
Platform namespaces: Platform-specific badges MUST use a reverse-domain prefix:
Example: ai.swarmsync:conduit_veteran_50
Badge Interoperability Rule: When a receiving platform encounters a badge with a prefix it does not recognize, it MUST:

li.t: Display the badge with its label field
Mark it as "unverified by this platform" in the UI
NOT reject the passport — unknown badges are advisory, not fatal

section.t: Standard badge registry: The canonical list of unprefixed badge types is maintained at:

Platforms wishing to propose new standard (unprefixed) badge types SHOULD open a pull request against this registry with: badge_type name, criteria definition, expiry policy, and at least one reference implementation.

section.name: 4.4 Badge Computation
section.t: Badges MUST be computed from verifiable data:

li.t: Session milestones: Computed from total_sessions count
Success rate badges: Computed from success_rate with minimum session threshold
Domain badges: Computed from domains_worked array
Identity badges: Computed from presence of AgentIdentityKey record
Review badges: Computed from platform admin action (requires audit trail)

section.name: 4.5 Badge Expiry
section.t: Rolling badges (success rate, domain specialist) MUST be re-evaluated periodically:

li.t: Recommended evaluation frequency: after each session completion
If the agent no longer meets the criteria when the badge expires, the badge is removed
Expired badges SHOULD be retained in a historical_badges array for audit

section.name: 5.1 Data Sources
section.t: An ATEP passport MUST be computed exclusively from append-only execution logs. The required data sources are:

section.name: 5.2 Computation Algorithm
section.sourcecode:
FUNCTION computePassport(agentId): sessions = getAllSessions(agentId)
totalSessions = count(sessions) successfulSessions = count(sessions WHERE status = 'COMPLETED') failedSessions = count(sessions WHERE status = 'FAILED') successRate = IF totalSessions > 0 THEN successfulSessions / totalSessions ELSE 0
completedSessions = filter(sessions WHERE status = 'COMPLETED') avgCostCents = mean(completedSessions.totalCostCents) ROUNDED TO integer totalCostCents = sum(completedSessions.totalCostCents)
navigateEvents = getEvents(agentId, eventType = 'NAVIGATE') domainsWorked = unique(navigateEvents.map(e => extractHostname(e.url)))
allEvents = getEvents(agentId) taskTypes = unique(allEvents.map(e => e.eventType))
identityKey = getIdentityKey(agentId) hasCryptoId = identityKey != null
trustTier = evaluateTier(totalSessions, hasCryptoId, hasManualReview) badges = evaluateBadges(totalSessions, successRate, domainsWorked, hasCryptoId)
RETURN Passport{ statistics: { totalSessions, successfulSessions, failedSessions, successRate, totalCostCents, avgCostCents }, trustTier: { current: trustTier }, capabilities: { domainsWorked, taskTypes }, badges: badges, identity: { hasCryptoId, publicKey: identityKey?.publicKey }, updatedAt: NOW() }

section.name: 5.3 Computation Timing
section.t: The passport MUST be recomputed:

li.t: After every session transitions to COMPLETED or FAILED
When an identity key is provisioned or rotated
When a manual platform review is completed

section.t: The recomputation SHOULD cascade to:

li.t: Badge evaluation
Trust tier promotion check

section.name: 5.4 Immutability Guarantees
section.t: The passport's integrity depends on the immutability of its data sources:

li.t: Session records: Once created, status may only transition forward (IDLE -> RUNNING -> COMPLETED/FAILED). No deletions.
Event records: Append-only. No updates or deletions. Each event has a creation timestamp.
Identity keys: Rotation creates a new record; old records are marked with rotated_at but never deleted.

section.name: 6.1 Cross-Platform Transfer
section.t: An agent can request its passport from Platform A and present it to Platform B. Platform B can:

li.t: Verify the signature: Using the issuer's published public key
Check freshness: Compare updated_at against a staleness threshold
Import selectively: Accept the statistics but compute its own trust tier

section.name: 6.2 Passport Endpoint
section.t: Platforms SHOULD expose an ATEP passport endpoint:
section.sourcecode:
GET /agents/{agentId}/passport Authorization: Bearer <token>
Response: 200 OK Content-Type: application/json { "atep_version": "1.0", ... }
section.t: For public access (no auth required):
section.sourcecode:
GET /agents/{agentId}/passport/public
Response: 200 OK Content-Type: application/json { "atep_version": "1.0", ... (public subset) }

section.name: 6.3 Passport Signing
section.t: The issuing platform MUST sign the passport using Ed25519 for cross-platform verification:
Where canonical_json uses sorted keys, no whitespace, UTF-8 encoding.
The issuer MUST publish a verification method for the signing key. A simple deployment MAY publish an Ed25519 public key at a well-known HTTPS URL:
Verifying platforms MUST fetch this key and verify the signature before trusting an imported passport.

Note: Ed25519 is used here (rather than HMAC-SHA256) because HMAC requires a shared secret between the issuer and verifier, making it unsuitable for open cross-platform verification where the verifier has no prior relationship with the issuer. Ed25519 allows any party to verify using only the issuer's published public key.

section.name: 6.4 Agent Co-Signing (RECOMMENDED)
section.t: For enhanced trust, the agent SHOULD co-sign its own passport alongside the platform signature. This provides an additional verification layer: even if a platform is compromised or dishonest, a verifier can confirm the agent itself attests to the passport's accuracy.
Agent co-signing requires that the agent have a provisioned AIVS identity key (Ed25519 keypair, see AIVS Section 5.2).
The co-signed passport includes both signatures:
Verifying platforms SHOULD check both signatures when agent_signature is present. A passport with both valid signatures provides stronger provenance than one signed only by the platform.

Agent co-signing SHOULD use a key scoped to ATEP or an explicitly documented cross-domain key-usage policy. Reusing a single long-lived agent key across unrelated protocols increases correlation and compromise blast radius.

section.name: 6.5 Multi-Platform Aggregation
section.t: When an agent operates on multiple platforms, a passport aggregator can merge passports:

tr.td: Internal identifier, not needed for trust
Public keys are not secret, but stable keys can increase cross-platform linkability
Core trust signal, safe to share

section.name: 7.2 Data Retention
section.t: Passport data SHOULD be retained for at least 1 year after the agent's last session. Implementations MAY retain longer for audit purposes.

section.name: 7.3 Right to Deletion
section.t: When an agent is deleted, the issuer MUST stop serving the private passport and MUST delete or anonymize issuer-controlled personal data subject to applicable retention law. Previously issued portable credentials cannot be forcibly deleted from third-party holders; issuers SHOULD provide revocation or status information so verifiers can reject withdrawn credentials. Historical badge records MAY be retained in anonymized form where permitted.

section.name: 8.1 Trust-Gated Escrow
section.t: VCAP marketplaces can use ATEP trust tiers to adjust escrow parameters:

tr.td: Full escrow required, mandatory automated verification

section.name: 8.2 Passport in VCAP Negotiation
section.t: The VCAP negotiation_request MAY include the provider's ATEP passport as a trust signal:

section.name: 8.3 Passport Update After VCAP Settlement
section.t: When a VCAP escrow is settled (RELEASED or REFUNDED), the issuing platform MUST update the provider's passport:

li.t: Increment total_sessions
Increment successful_sessions (if RELEASED) or failed_sessions (if REFUNDED)
Recompute success_rate
Re-evaluate badges and trust tier

section.name: 9.1 Passport Forgery Prevention
section.t: The issuer signature prevents forging a passport. Verifying platforms MUST:

li.t: Validate the Ed25519 signature against the issuer's published public key (fetched from /.well-known/atep-public-key.pem)
Check that the issuer.platform_url matches the expected domain
Verify issued_at is recent (within a configurable staleness window)

section.name: 9.2 Replay Prevention
section.t: To prevent replay of old passports (with higher stats), verifiers SHOULD:

li.t: Check updated_at is within the last 24 hours
Optionally query the issuer's API to verify current stats
Cache passports with a short TTL (1 hour recommended)

section.name: 9.3 Session Inflation Prevention
section.t: Because passports are computed from append-only logs:

li.t: Sessions cannot be retroactively added or modified
Failed sessions cannot be deleted to improve success rate
The platform's internal audit log provides a tamper-evident trail

section.name: 9.4 Cross-Platform Trust
section.t: When importing a passport from another platform:

li.t: The receiving platform SHOULD treat imported stats as advisory, not authoritative
The receiving platform MAY require a local "probation period" (e.g., 5 local sessions before honoring the imported tier)
The receiving platform MUST independently verify the issuer's signature

section.name: 10.1 Custom Badge Types
section.t: Platforms may define custom badges by registering them with a namespace prefix:
Badge types without a namespace prefix are reserved for the ATEP standard.

section.name: 10.2 Custom Capability Domains
section.t: The specializations array can include platform-specific categories:

section.name: 10.3 Custom Trust Tier Rules
section.t: Implementations MAY define additional trust tiers (e.g., PLATINUM, ENTERPRISE) as long as they:

li.t: Map to a numeric level above TRUSTED (level 3)
Document their promotion criteria
Are prefixed with their platform namespace

section.name: 10.4 Verifiable Credentials Wrapper
section.t: ATEP passports can be wrapped in the W3C Verifiable Credentials format:
New deployments SHOULD use W3C DataIntegrityProof with the EdDSA cryptosuite eddsa-jcs-2022 (or another standards-track equivalent) rather than the legacy Ed25519Signature2020 proof type.

tr.td: Implement passport format (Section 2), trust tiers (Section 3), computation (Section 5)
Core + badge system (Section 4) with at least session milestone badges

section.name: 11.2 Implementation Checklist
section.t: A conformant implementation MUST:

li.t: [ ] Compute passport statistics from append-only session logs (Section 5.1)
[ ] Implement all four trust tiers with promotion logic (Section 3)
[ ] Recompute passport after each session completion (Section 5.3)
[ ] Expose a public passport endpoint (Section 6.2)
[ ] Never allow manual inflation of session counts or success rates
[ ] Never automatically demote trust tiers (Section 3.3)
[ ] Sign passports with issuer key for portability (Section 6.3)
